title: Planarian head number is not directly encoded in the genome

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Planarian head number is not directly encoded in the genome

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: How many heads a planarian cellular collective produces is not directly encoded in its genome, since the same wild-type cells can produce 1-, 2- or 0-headed planaria depending on their history; the genome encodes the hardware (e.g. ion channels) while the outcome results from experience-sensitive electrophysiological 'software'.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Re-writing morphogenetic memories: ontogenetic and evolutionary timescales

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The question, of how many heads a given cellular collective will produce, is, surprisingly, not directly encoded in its genome because exactly the same, wild-type set of cells can produce 1-, 2-, or 0-headed planaria depending on their history.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Re-writing morphogenetic memories: ontogenetic and evolutionary timescales”. Scope: Planarian flatworms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Context-dependent head number in wild-type material is measurable and testable. It does not uniquely support the hardware-software interpretation or show that genomic information is irrelevant, so the conceptual claim is only partially resolved.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Show that genetically matched planarian cells generate zero, one, or two heads under documented physiological histories, and quantify how well genotype alone versus genotype plus physiological state predicts head number. Poor genotype-only prediction supports context dependence, not literal absence of genomic influence.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The genome can encode a context-sensitive reaction norm without fixing one outcome.

Matched sequence, history, voltage, and morphology data are scarce.

'Directly encoded' is ambiguous.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.58
analysis feasibility: 0.72
operationalizability: 0.62
data adequacy: 0.48
discriminating power: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Whether head number varies at a fixed genotype is an empirical contrast, and the published physiological manipulations report one-, two-, and zero-headed outcomes from wild-type stocks. Those results are paper-level measurements, not a sequence-plus-phenotype matrix. The software metaphor adds no further observable beyond that genotype-phenotype dissociation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Hold genotype fixed, by wild-type stock plus reversibility or by sequencing, and record regenerative head number after different physiological histories. One, two, and zero heads from the same genotype would support head number not being a direct function of the genome; a genetic variant necessary for each deviant head number would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Wild-type is usually inferred from stock history and reversibility, not from deposited genomes of the zero- and two-headed animals.

History can include microbiome and chromatin changes that are still encoded outcomes of the genome's regulatory capacities.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.75
data adequacy: 0.5
data existence: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.5
